record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Is there a pure morphic binary word avoiding 2-abelian cubes?

evidence.quote: Is there a pure morphic binary word avoiding 2-abelian cubes?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and $\Sigma^*$ the free monoid of finite words over $\Sigma$. For an integer $k\ge 1$, two finite words $u,v\in\Sigma^*$ are said to be $k$-abelian equivalent, written $u\sim_k v$, if for every word $f\in\Sigma^*$ with $|f|\le k$, the number of occurrences of $f$ as a (contiguous) factor of $u$ equals the number of occurrences of $f$ as a factor of $v$. (For $k=1$ this is ordinary abelian equivalence, i.e.\ equality of Parikh vectors.)

A $k$-abelian cube is a non-empty word of the form $u_1 u_2 u_3$ with $u_1\sim_k u_2 \sim_k u_3$ and $|u_1|=|u_2|=|u_3|\ge 1$. An infinite word $\mathbf{w}\in\Sigma^{\mathbb{N}}$ avoids $k$-abelian cubes if no factor of $\mathbf{w}$ is a $k$-abelian cube.

A morphism is a map $h:\Sigma^*\to\Sigma^*$ satisfying $h(xy)=h(x)h(y)$. Given a letter $a\in\Sigma$ such that $h(a)=ax$ for some non-empty $x\in\Sigma^*$ and such that $|h^n(a)|\to\infty$, the unique infinite fixed point $h^\omega(a)=\lim_{n\to\infty}h^n(a)$ is called a pure morphic word. (No coding is applied; the alphabet of the infinite word equals $\Sigma$.)

Problem. Take $\Sigma=\{0,1\}$. Does there exist a pure morphic infinite binary word $\mathbf{w}\in\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}$ that avoids $2$-abelian cubes?
artifact.category_tag: Combinatorics on words / abelian pattern avoidance
artifact.status_search_result: It is known that 2-abelian cubes are avoidable on a binary alphabet (Rao–Rosenfeld and related works show k-abelian cubes are avoidable on binary alphabets for k ≥ 2). However, whether such an avoiding word can be realized as a pure morphic word (the fixed point of a binary morphism, with no coding) does not appear to be settled in the literature; results for the analogous ternary k-abelian-square problem show that pure morphic constructions face genuine obstructions, and no construction or impossibility proof for the binary 2-abelian-cube case was found in the search.

status_evidence.title: 5-abelian cubes are avoidable on binary alphabets
status_evidence.snippet: k-abelian cubes are avoidable over a binary alphabet for k ≥ 8, and then it was proved that this holds for k ≥ 5.
status_evidence.claim: Avoidability of k-abelian cubes on binary alphabets has been progressively established for smaller k, with 2-abelian cubes shown avoidable on the binary alphabet, but the question of pure morphic constructions remains separate.

status_evidence.title: 3-Abelian Cubes Are Avoidable on Binary Alphabets
status_evidence.snippet: 3-abelian cubes are avoidable on binary alphabets.
status_evidence.claim: Successive strengthenings have been published, indicating active research; pure-morphic versions are not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Rosenfeld thesis
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of k-abelian avoidability and morphic constructions.
status_evidence.claim: Pure morphic avoidance of k-abelian repetitions is a delicate, restricted setting; binary 2-abelian-cube case not resolved here.
